thread:
sara: quick follow-up from the FROG outage postmortem. we captured a few action items but they need concrete owners and dates. can we surface a lightweight tracking approach?

mike: +1. i think our current tracker is too free-form. missed a couple of reminders last time.

alyssa: proposal: single canonical follow-up doc per postmortem, with a one-line owner + due date for each item. exportable to the oncall tracker.

jordan: sounds good. also we should identify recurring patterns across incidents (eg: db failover triggers) and track them as "cluster issues" not one-off tasks.

sara: agreed. my main ask: who will own the remediation and what is the SLA for follow-up? 14 days for low/medium and 72 hours for high?

mike: 72h for high seems fine. but we need a template so folks don't debate formats. something like: 

```
- summary: short description
- impact: customers affected + severity
- owner: @username
- due: YYYY-MM-DD
- action: brief steps / deliverable
- status: todo / in-progress / blocked / done
- followups: links to PRs / runbooks
```

alyssa: love that. I'd add a recurring-incident flag and a short field: recurrence_notes.

oncall-bot: reminder: postmortem FROG-2025-07 requires owner assignment within 48 hours.

sara: thanks bot. @mike can you take ownership of the infra-related items? there are two: kernel tuning and autoscaler tweak.

mike: i can own kernel tuning (due 2025-07-30). autoscaler tweak depends on load tests; assigning to @alyssa for test plan (due 2025-07-25).

alyssa: ack. will draft test plan this week.

jordan: i'll take responsibility for synthesizing recurring patterns from the last 6 months and produce a short slide deck. due 2025-08-05.

sara: awesome. next: comms cadence. during outage we had many overlapping pings. proposal: incident comms owner posts updates at T+15, T+45, T+90 unless there's a status change.

mike: i like that. makes expectations clear. add a line to the template: comms_owner and cadence.

alyssa: also rotation for incident commander. current rotation is ad-hoc. suggest a 2-week IC rotation with pager overlap one day for handoff.

sam: real quick — would ops oncall still be first responder, and IC escalates? want to be clear on call flow.

jordan: yes. ops oncall is triage/mitigation first 30m, then IC takes over full coordination if incident meets severity threshold. documenting flow in the playbook helps new folks.

sara: ok actionables we captured here:
- add follow-up template to postmortem checklist (owner: alyssa, due: 2025-07-22)
- create automatic reminders in oncall tracker for 72h/14d depending on severity (owner: mike, due: 2025-07-24)
- tag recurring incidents and create quarterly "cluster issues" list (owner: jordan, due: 2025-08-05)
- update incident playbook with comms cadence + IC rotation (owner: sara, due: 2025-07-28)

mike: can we add a lightweight column in the tracker for risk-to-customer? helps prioritize follow-ups.

alyssa: yes — risk (low/med/high) fits our triage process. add to template.

oncall-bot: created task FROG-POSTM-1 assigned to alyssa, due 2025-07-22.

sara: perfect. let's reconvene in weekly oncall sync on Thursday to ensure these are progressing. if anyone needs help with timelines, ping me directly.

sam: thanks, all. small ask: can we auto-generate a timeline snippet for the postmortem doc from incident logs? that would speed drafting.

jordan: we have a quick script that pulls events from the incident log. i'll PR a helper to the docs repo this week.

mike: final note — measure compliance: after 30 days, we'll report % of postmortem items closed on time. put that in monthly ops review.

sara: noted. adding compliance metric to our ops dashboard. :thumbsup:

alyssa: i'll update the template and open the PR to the postmortem checklist by EOD Friday.

sara: thanks everyone — closing thread when first task is created.
